title: Allow serve to enable embedded dashboard through explicit CLI overrides
description:
Cacophony's separately supervised Pi Daemon host is headless/Unix-socket-only, while the machine-level instance exposes the useful browser dashboard. Pi Daemon `serve` already accepts API CLI flags, but embedded web enablement/bind/port is currently read only from Pi Daemon YAML; `serve` rejects web CLI options.

Add explicit, typed CLI overrides for embedded web on `pi-daemon serve` so supervisors can configure one self-describing process without generating an extra side config file.

Required surface (names may follow existing config vocabulary):

- `--web-enabled true|false`
- `--web-bind HOST`
- `--web-port PORT`
- optional `--public-origin URL` only if required by the existing embedded dashboard contract
- embedded mode only for `serve`; reject a requested dedicated mode rather than spawning a hidden second process

Semantics/security:

- omitted options preserve current behavior exactly;
- web bind defaults to literal loopback and the first Cacophony canary uses loopback only;
- option-like web values are validated with the same constraints as Pi Daemon's YAML/web command path;
- explicit disable overrides enabling YAML, matching `--api-enabled false` behavior;
- embedded dashboard uses the same resident multiplexer/session catalog and shows logical sessions from this host instance;
- no bearer bytes on argv; API auth remains `--api-token-file`, token fd, env, or generated owner-only `STATE_DIR/api-token` under existing mutual-exclusion rules;
- help, docs and startup/status output identify API and web addresses without exposing token contents;
- clean shutdown covers dashboard server as today.

Acceptance:

1. `serve` with omitted web flags stays socket/API-only according to existing config.
2. `serve --web-enabled true --web-bind 127.0.0.1 --web-port <free>` starts the embedded dashboard and serves the same logical-session inventory as the Unix/API host.
3. Explicit false overrides enabling YAML.
4. Invalid port/bind and incompatible mode combinations fail before publishing listeners.
5. API + web on distinct loopback ports starts and shuts down cleanly; token file stays 0600 and is never logged.
6. Tests prove CLI overrides and YAML precedence without binding public interfaces.
7. A Cacophony consumer can capability-gate the new flags by pinned source revision/version.

This is the upstream half of Cacophony-managed Pi Daemon dashboard observability. The machine-level daemon-main instance on ports 7463/7465 must remain independent.

Implementation checkpoint before broad edits (2026-08-01): precedence will be explicit --web-enabled > YAML web.enabled; explicit --web-bind/--web-port > YAML > existing loopback/default values. Unlike API, --web-port alone will not imply enablement: web exposure stays explicit. Explicit false disables YAML true. serve --web-enabled true rejects YAML mode: dedicated. CLI override validation must complete before Unix/API/web listeners publish. First focused test added before implementation: serve CLI enables embedded Dashboard when YAML omits web; current source is red as expected (1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail; options rejected before lifecycle callback).

title: adapterReadiness reports green from configured credentials, never from a working call
description:
## `adapterReadiness` reports green from CONFIGURED credentials, never from a working call

Observed live on ms-dev (pi-daemon 0.2.2), then traced and confirmed **still present on current main
(0.3.0)**, so this is not fixed by the pending 0.2.2 -> 0.3.0 rollout.

### Live evidence
Host `status` reported, with no session ever opened:
```
adapterReadiness: { ready: true, configuredProviderCount: 5, availableModels: 69,
                    authenticatedModels: 69, authErrorCount: 0, authErrorCodes: [] }
```
Two logical sessions were then opened and driven to a real turn. Every turn failed:
```
stopReason: "error", content: [], usage.totalTokens: 0
errorMessage: Azure OpenAI API error (401): Access denied due to invalid subscription key
              or wrong API endpoint.
```
Readiness stayed `ready: true, authenticatedModels: 69, authErrorCount: 0` throughout.

### Mechanism, on main
`src/pi-adapter.ts:218`
```ts
const authenticatedModels = available.filter((model) =>
  runtime.hasConfiguredAuth(model.provider),
).length;
```
`authenticatedModels` counts models whose provider has credentials **configured**, not credentials
that **work**. The field name asserts a property the computation never checks.

`authErrorCount` / `authErrorCodes` exist and would express exactly this, but `#recordAuthError`
(`src/pi-adapter.ts:186`) is only reachable from startup credential resolution
(`listCredentials()` catch at :173, and the init-error path at :180). No call-time auth failure ever
reaches it, so `authErrorCount` cannot leave 0 once the process has started, and
`ready` (`:222`, `registryError === undefined && authenticatedModels > 0`) cannot go false for bad
credentials.

### Why it matters beyond cosmetics
This readiness field is what an operator and any monitoring path consult to answer "is the host
usable". It answered "yes, 69/69 authenticated" for ~23 hours while the host could not complete a
single turn. In the incident that surfaced this (cacophony:bd-ea3487), that false green is a large
part of why the investigation looked elsewhere: the host advertised full capacity and zero auth
errors while failing every request.

### Suggested shape
Feed call-time auth failures back into the same accounting the struct already has: when a turn fails
with an authentication/authorization error, record the code via the existing `#recordAuthError` path
so `authErrorCount` becomes non-zero and `ready` degrades. That needs no wire change — the fields are
already published.

If instead the intended meaning is "credentials are configured", the field is misnamed and should say
so (`credentialedModels`), so nothing downstream reads it as proof that calls will succeed.

### Not verified by me
I did not attempt the fix. I have no way to exercise a live 401 against a locally built 0.3.0 from
here, and guessing at auth accounting in a codebase I have just met is the same class of error this
bead is about. Evidence and line references above are exact; the design call belongs to this project.

Filed from cacophony:bd-ea3487 (pi-daemon hosting was dead fleet-wide; separate root cause was a
config path defect, now fixed there). Related: bd-99577e, which notes `status` does not report the
model a session is bound to — the same session in this evidence also ignored the `model` supplied at
`open` on 0.2.2 and ran the host default, which is worth checking against 0.3.0 where
`multiplexer.ts:2246/2347` does carry `payload.model` through.

title: [broken-on-main] nix flake check fails: e2e-shell guard rejects the store path it must accept
description:
`nix flake check` fails on main. The `e2e-shell` check throws during evaluation:

```
error: e2e-shell-check: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH carries a store-path reference.
```

Present since ddf077c and invisible until 6dffafe unblocked CI dispatch, so it was red from the moment it landed rather than regressing later.

Cause, and it is a process failure rather than a design one. While verifying the string-context guard I mutated the file to remove `builtins.unsafeDiscardStringContext`, confirmed the guard fired, then "restored" it with `git checkout nix/e2e-shell-check.nix` — which restores from the index, and I had already `git add`ed the mutated version. So the restore was a no-op. The verification that should have caught it ran `nix build ... | tail -1 && echo restored`, where the pipeline's exit status is `tail`'s, so the `&&` fired on a failing build. The commit was then amended from that index. The negative-control mutation shipped as the change.

Two independent mistakes, both of which had to hold: a revert that did not revert, and a check of the wrong exit status.

There is also a real design fault underneath, identified by a reviewer. Composing guard with discard is vacuous: `noContext "..." (unsafeDiscardStringContext x)` can never throw, because the discard guarantees the value has no context. It would have looked protective while asserting nothing — the same vacuity class this session has been about, this time inside the guard written to enforce it.

Fix: the guard applies only to values that should never carry context — `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD`, `PI_DAEMON_PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_VERSION`, and the `@playwright/test` pin. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` is a store path by nature, so it is the documented exception: its context is discarded explicitly, with a comment saying why it is exempt, and its shape is still asserted by `validate` against `/nix/store/*playwright-browsers*`.

title: Give the suite a deliberate source of environment variation, and scope what that can and cannot catch
description:
Proposed after four vacuous assertions were found in one night, none by review. Filed as a draft because the design question below is unresolved and worth deciding before anyone builds it.

The observation, from an agent who converged on it independently: every instance was exposed by an environment differing from the authoring one, and none by reading the test. The convention filed as bd-c9c453 tells authors to demonstrate that an assertion can fail, but the mechanism that actually caught these was variation, and the project has no deliberate source of it.

Honest accounting of what a variation lane would have caught, because the case is weaker than it first looks. The four instances:

1. A credential fixture whose permissiveness depended on the runner's umask. Caught by `umask 077`. Cheap and mechanical.
2. A Rich/TUI reading-anchor assertion that compared two pre-hydration values. Needed real CPU contention, so partially reachable by running under load, but the specific window was timing-dependent and would not reproduce reliably.
3. A test pinning an exact npm script string, broken when a preflight was legitimately inserted. Not environmental at all — it took another agent editing the pipeline.
4. Flake source-text assertions that survived an alejandra reformat by luck. Also not environmental — it took a formatter run.

So an environment matrix addresses one and a half of four. That is still worth having, but the framing should be wider than environment: what exposes a vacuous assertion is *departure from the conditions it was written under*, and environment is only one axis. Editing (3) and tooling (4) are the others, and both were supplied here by a second agent doing unrelated work — which is a form of variation the project gets for free from parallelism and cannot rely on when a file has one owner.

Concrete proposal for the mechanical part, deliberately narrow:

- One CI job running the existing Node suite unchanged under a varied environment: `umask 077`, a timezone far from UTC, `LANG=C`, and a constrained `/dev/shm`. Not a new suite and no new assertions — the same tests, different conditions. This is the piece that would have caught (1) outright.
- It should be advisory before it is required. A new axis of variation will surface pre-existing latent assumptions, and turning those into a blocking gate on day one converts a useful signal into pressure to skip tests.

Open questions worth settling first:

- Which axes are worth their runtime, given the project already has three lanes and a macOS job that times out at 25 minutes.
- Whether load-based variation is worth attempting at all, given (2) was found on a shared host by accident and a deliberate loop was argued down earlier tonight on the grounds that the loop changes the load it is measuring.
- Whether the editing and tooling axes can be addressed at all by CI, or whether they are inherently what review and parallel work provide.

Discovered while implementing bd-58a7fa; the convention it follows from is bd-c9c453.

## Folded in from bd-d09b2b, closed as a duplicate of this bead

Two additions from that version, both accepted:

- ~~**Process uid as an axis, alongside umask.**~~ **Withdrawn — see bd-9ad9e5.** Investigated after being proposed, and it argues against itself. The owner-mismatch guards are real and largely untested (41 of them across 21 files, with no test found for the errors they raise), but they are not reachable by a variation lane: running the suite as a different uid does not help, because the fixtures are created by that same uid, so the comparison stays equal. Running as root fails for the same reason. The guard is unreachable by construction in any design where the process that creates the fixture is the process that loads it, which is every lane the project has or could cheaply add. It needs privileged fixture setup, which does not belong in the standard gate, or form 2 from bd-c9c453 — extract the predicate and check in the cases it should reject. Recorded here as a correction rather than removed silently, because "uid is an obvious next axis" is an appealing wrong answer and the reason it fails is not obvious.
- **`PI_DAEMON_PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS` as the precedent for advisory-then-required.** The shape is already in the tree and already accepted: the measurement always runs and prints, and only the assertion is gated behind the switch. A variation lane can do the same — always run and report, gate later — which supplies the advisory phase without inventing a second mechanism.

## Resolved: leave load out

The open question on load-based variation is settled against including it. The reading-anchor instance was found under load-13 contention on a shared host, but what made it diagnosable was instrumenting the pane in a real browser; the load reported that something was wrong without indicating what, and both agents who looked at it spent longer on plausible wrong hypotheses than on the fix. A deliberate load axis would reproduce that experience without reproducing the instrumentation that actually resolved it. Earlier in the same session a load-hunting retry loop was argued down on the related ground that the loop changes the load it is measuring.

That leaves the proposed axes as: umask, timezone, locale, and constrained `/dev/shm`. Uid was considered and withdrawn; see above and bd-9ad9e5.

title: Make a stale dist distinguishable from a real failure in the build-free test loop
description:
`npm run test:unit` runs the Node suite without building, which makes it the
obvious fast loop, but it silently runs against whatever `dist/` happens to
contain. Earlier in this session that produced:

    SyntaxError: The requested module '../dist/pi-sdk-contract.js' does not
    provide an export named 'PI_SDK_EXPORTS_DEFAULT_SESSION_DIR'

The code was correct; a peer had landed that export and the local `dist/` simply
predated it. The message points at a module that looks broken rather than at a
stale build, which is a plausible route to misfiling a broken-on-main bead.

bd-acd227 added `test:src`, which compiles first and is nearly as fast, so the
foot-gun is now avoidable. What is missing is anything that tells you which one
you are in. Options, roughly in order of value:

1. Have `test:unit` compare a cheap fingerprint of `src/**` against one written
   into `dist/` at build time, and warn (not fail) when they differ. The
   existing `src/source-fingerprint.ts` may already provide the primitive.
2. Failing that, a line in CONTRIBUTING next to `test:unit` naming the hazard
   and pointing at `test:src`.

Deliberately not proposing that `test:unit` build: its whole value is not
building. The gap is that a stale run is indistinguishable from a real failure.

title: The published integration example receives no events: it never attaches
description:
`docs/integration.md` publishes the consumer example Cacophony follows: connect, `client.subscribe(event => ...)` with a `messageUpdate` comment, then `open`, then `wake`. A client doing exactly that receives no events at all.

`docs/protocol.md:81` states the actual rule: "Event delivery is explicit. `open`, `wake`, `status`, `abort`, successful commands, and failed commands never subscribe a connection implicitly. A client must send `attach` with the current `sessionId` and `generation` before it expects events." The behaviour is deliberate and correct; the integration guide simply never mentions `attach`, and its `client.subscribe` line reads as though registering a listener is sufficient.

Measured against a live model rather than inferred, `github-copilot/gemini-3-flash-preview`, two concurrent sessions:

    documented sequence (open, wake)          eventCounts { a: 0, b: 0 }
    with attach between open and wake         eventCounts { a: 14, b: 14 }

`attach` also requires `payload: {}`; omitting it fails validation with `invalid_field: payload`, which the guide would need to show or a reader hits immediately.

The second half is why nobody noticed. `scripts/live-sdk-smoke.mjs` — the only end-to-end check against a real model — records `eventCounts` in its report and never asserts them. It has been printing zeros through every run, including the migration verification earlier tonight, and a zero in a printed report is not a failing test.

So: add `attach` to the integration example with the payload and a sentence on explicit delivery, and make the live smoke assert that events arrive rather than merely counting them. Then a regression in event delivery fails the check that exists to catch it.

title: Prove zero process creation per logical session against a served daemon
description:
`PLAN.md` §"End-to-end consumer" is still open: a Cacophony-facing acceptance that launches the packaged service, creates multiple logical agents, wakes them, and proves no new process appears per wake. It is the property Cacophony deploys this daemon for — one supervised process replacing repeated `pico --resume` / `pi --mode rpc` process creation — and it is currently proven only in-process.

`test/full-host-acceptance.test.mjs` instruments `child_process` inside the test process and forbids spawning, which is strong evidence about the code path but says nothing about the served artefact: the daemon under test is constructed in-process, not started as a process a supervisor would run. A Cacophony deployment gets the latter.

Credential-free slice, which is the half that can land without a live provider:

- start `dist/cli.js serve` as a real child on a temporary socket, state dir, and agent dir, exactly as `test/bootstrap-cli.test.mjs` does;
- connect over the protocol socket and open several logical sessions;
- sample the daemon's descendants from the OS process table before and after, and assert the count is unchanged.

Session creation is the expensive operation Cacophony repeats today, so proving it costs no process is the load-bearing half. The wake half needs either a live provider or a fixture the served daemon can be pointed at, and belongs with the opt-in live SDK path rather than in credential-free CI.

Worth being explicit about what the slice does not prove, so the summary does not overclaim: it establishes zero process creation per logical session through a real process boundary, not per wake, and not through the Nix package. Those are separate follow-ups.

title: Retain a structured browser-suite run record so a local failure classifies itself
description:
A local full browser-suite failure is currently unclassifiable after the fact, because nothing retains the run output. This is not hypothetical: a full-suite run on sonance failed six scenarios in under a second each, and by the time anyone wanted to test what caused it the output was gone, so it could not be distinguished between two candidate mechanisms with different fixes — host starvation, or the browser dying at launch. The latter has a specific signature, `browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed` against every scenario, which is exactly what the CI runner produced in run 30412617437 for bd-df1c84. Five subsequent local runs did not reproduce it.

CI already retains its evidence: the `Dash browser smoke` job uploads `web/test-results` and `web/playwright-report` on failure. A local run has no equivalent, so a one-in-six event is lost rather than recorded.

Proposal, from the agent whose incident this was: add a JSON reporter alongside `list` in `web/playwright.config.ts`, writing to `web/test-results/run.json`. Rationale for the reporter rather than teeing console output — it captures each scenario's error text structurally, which is the property that makes the next occurrence self-classifying, and it avoids ANSI escapes, `pipefail` fragility, and interleaved output. Playwright already writes traces to that directory on failure, so the run record lands beside them, and the directory is already gitignored. Cost on a passing run is effectively zero.

Also add one line to `docs/dash-e2e.md` telling a future investigator to read `web/test-results/run.json` first, and check whether `run.json` should be included in the CI artifact upload for the same reason.

Filed at the request of pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son, who will claim and implement it; their `caco bd create` was returning indeterminately against a flapping helsinki, and under create-only cross-project scope a duplicate could not be seen or closed afterwards. title: Reorder the negative-control forms and record what direct observation costs
description:
The negative-control convention landed in `4910781` (bd-27c44a) lists three
forms in the wrong order, and is missing two constraints found in review.

**Ordering.** It currently reaches for a checked-in negative case first and a
checked precondition second. Review by pidm-pi-on-demand-dev-test-son identified
the flaw: a manual mutation, and to a lesser extent an enumerated negative case,
is exercised in the environment the author is already in. For the umask instance
that is the benign one — deliberately breaking the fail-closed property under a
permissive umask shows the assertion firing correctly, so the ritual passes and
confirms a test that is vacuous elsewhere. A checked precondition fails in
precisely the environment that would otherwise hollow the test out, including
environments nobody on the project has. So it should be first.

Stated narrowly rather than as dominance, because the two forms answer different
questions and neither implies the other: a precondition check proves the setup
still establishes the situation the assertion needs; a negative case proves the
predicate still rejects. The precondition form goes first because it catches
vacuity the author cannot enumerate, not because it subsumes the alternative.

**Missing caveat: what direct observation drags in.** "Assert the effect, not
the spelling" is cheap to state and can be expensive to follow. Interpolating a
store path such as `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` into a check derivation puts that
closure into the check's build inputs — 2.1 GiB of Playwright on every
`nix flake check` in the concrete case. The observation needs its string context
discarded, or the check confined to attributes carrying no store path. Worth
stating, because nobody would guess that observing a value can pull a bundle
into a gate that previously did not need it.

**Missing caveat: lanes.** Direct observation is only free if the lane running
the assertion can perform it. Evaluating a devShell attribute needs Nix, and the
Node gate deliberately has none, so preferring the stronger form can mean moving
an assertion between lanes rather than rewriting it in place.

Scope: reorder and rewrite the CONTRIBUTING section, update
`test/permission-fixture.test.mjs` which asserts the section's shape, and cite
the `playwright-browser-resolution` conversion as the worked example for form 1
once it lands.

title: Run the suite under deliberate environmental variation, starting with umask
description:
Four assertions were found vacuous in one session, in four unrelated areas. The
convention landed tonight (`CONTRIBUTING`, "Negative controls", bd-27c44a /
bd-c9c453 / bd-318c09) tells an author how to demonstrate an assertion can fail.
It does not address how these were actually found, which is worth separating
because the answer is uncomfortable:

- the scroll assertion, by a loaded host (bd-94d7df);
- the umask fixture, by a hardened CI runner (bd-7cba4b);
- the pipeline string, by a legitimate addition to the pipeline (bd-228b91);
- the flake source match, by an alejandra reformat (bd-d79ef1).

None was found by reading the test, and none by review — including the two that
three agents reviewed carefully last night. Every one was found by an environment
differing from the authoring one, and in every case by accident.

So the project relies on environmental variation to find this class, and has no
deliberate source of it. The variation that did the work was incidental: someone
else's runner, host load, an unrelated formatting change.

Cheap deliberate sources, roughly in order of cost:

1. Run the Node suite once under a restrictive umask. That single variation
   would have caught the umask instance directly, and it costs one CI step. It
   is also the variation the project is most exposed to, since none of us has a
   hardened machine and the runners do.
2. Run once with a deliberately hostile `TMPDIR` mode, or as a different uid,
   for the same reason.
3. Consider whether the existing performance-budget switch is the right pattern:
   an opt-in environment that the standard gate does not pay for, but which a
   nightly or on-demand run exercises.

Not proposing mutation testing — too heavy for this codebase and mostly finds
what the negative-control convention already covers. The narrow claim is that
umask is a known, cheap, high-yield axis and we already have one confirmed
instance it would have caught.

title: An unresolvable model is accepted at open, contrary to the documented refusal
description:
`docs/integration.md` opens with a prerequisite section stating that opening a session "validates that credentials exist for the provider named in `model`, before any turn is attempted", and that a client naming one the instance has no entry for "is refused at `open`, not at `wake`".

Measured, not inferred. Against a freshly served daemon with an isolated state and agent directory:

  payload.model = { provider: "no-such-provider", id: "no-such-model" }
  -> open response ok: true, session created, state idle

So an unresolvable provider/model is accepted at open rather than refused.

`src/pi-adapter.ts:352-370` shows the mechanism. `modelRuntime.getModel(provider, id)` returns undefined for an unknown pair, and `model` then falls back through `scope.scopedModels[0]?.model` to `(await modelRuntime.getAvailable())[0]`. The auth check on the following line tests `model.provider` — the *substituted* model's provider — so it passes. The documented refusal fires only when the named provider resolves to a real model that lacks credentials.

What I verified: the open succeeds. What I did not verify, and what matters more: whether a subsequent wake then runs on the substituted model. `status` does not report the bound model, so confirming it needs a wake and an inspection of which model answered — a credentialed run I did not do rather than a conclusion I am asserting.

If it does substitute, the consequence for Cacophony is direct: it will name a model per agent, and a typo or a model the instance lacks would silently produce a session running on whatever is first available, with no error at open and a plausible answer at wake. That is worse than a refusal in exactly the way tonight's other findings were — the failure is indistinguishable from success from the client's side.

Three possible resolutions, and the choice is a product decision rather than a doc fix:

1. Refuse at open when `model` names a pair the runtime cannot resolve, which is what the guide already promises.
2. Keep the fallback and report the substitution in the open response, so a client can detect it.
3. Keep the behaviour and correct the guide, which currently tells integrators the opposite.

Whichever is chosen, `status` reporting the bound model would make the state observable, which it currently is not.


## Settled: it is silent substitution, measured by pidm-pi-on-demand

The open question above is answered. Opening with `{ provider: "no-such-provider", id: "no-such-model" }`, attaching, and waking with a real turn:

    OPEN ok: true
    WAKE ok: true   (no error)
    EVENTS: 11 | model refs: "provider":"anthropic", "model":"claude-fable-5"

So the turn runs, on a model from a provider the client never named, and nothing in the open response, the wake response, or `status` reports it. The identity was recoverable only by scanning the event stream.

That makes this a product defect rather than a documentation one: the implementation has drifted from the contract the guide states, and the drift is silent in both directions — the client cannot detect the substitution, and the service cannot tell that the client did not mean it.

Raising to P1. A per-agent model typo, or a model a particular instance happens not to carry, yields a working session answering from whatever that instance lists first. For a deployment that assigns models per agent this is a correctness failure that presents as success.

Two coherent resolutions; the choice is product semantics and is with the operator:

1. Refuse at open when `model` names a pair the runtime cannot resolve. This matches the guide's prerequisite section and the neutrality claim that the client provides model policy and the service does not choose one.
2. Substitute deliberately and report the bound model in the open response, so a client can detect and accept it.

Either way `status` should report the bound model, which it currently does not, so the state is observable rather than only inferable from events.

Interim: the guide is being corrected to describe what the implementation does today rather than a refusal that does not happen, without endorsing it as intended behaviour.

title: Acceptance: launch the packaged daemon as a service and drive the neutral consumer path
description:
PLAN.md section "End-to-end consumer" is unimplemented: "A later Cacophony integration test launches the Nix package as a service, creates multiple logical pico-daemon agents, wakes them, and proves no new process appears per wake."

Current coverage stops short of the artifact. Every protocol and session test runs against `dist/` in the source tree; the built package's only runtime exercise is `installCheckPhase` running `pi-daemon version`, and the home-manager check validates module wiring rather than runtime behaviour. So nothing launches the installed artifact as a service and drives the neutral protocol through it — which is the exact configuration a Cacophony node will deploy.

The wake half needs credentials and stays opt-in. The rest does not, and is worth having in the credential-free gate:

- launch `${package}/bin/pi-daemon serve` against a temporary owner-private state directory
- open several logical sessions over the Unix socket with distinct ids and generations
- exercise the neutral surfaces a consumer uses: subscribe, list, close, and the documented `PiDaemonClient` request shape from docs/integration.md
- assert the process count attributable to the daemon does not grow per session, which is the architectural claim the whole design rests on
- shut down cleanly and assert no orphaned children

Value beyond coverage: it tests the artifact rather than the working tree. The 0.82.1 migration shipped an untracked test helper that every local check passed over and only the Nix package build caught, because the builder sees a source-only tree. A packaged-service acceptance closes the same gap for runtime behaviour rather than for build inputs.

Scope note: this is consumer acceptance, permitted by PLAN.md line 613 as neutral compatibility fixtures and consumer acceptance. It imports nothing from Cacophony and models no bead, message, profile, or token.

title: Say where migration-time verification goes, since it stops meaning anything once the migration lands
description:
While adopting the ownership predicate I wrote a verification script, copied it
into `scripts/`, and then removed it again — which was the right call, but the
reasoning is worth capturing because the pull to keep it was strong.

The script derived each guard's expected policy from `origin/main` and compared
it against the converted source. It was genuinely useful: 44 sites, zero
mismatches, and it failed correctly when a policy was flipped on purpose. But it
compares against `origin/main`, so the moment the conversion lands, `origin/main`
contains the converted code and the comparison becomes vacuous. It would still
run, still pass, and mean nothing — the exact failure mode the convention landed
tonight exists to prevent, in a script rather than a test.

The repository has no convention about this, and the instinct to keep a script
that just did useful work is strong. `scripts/` currently holds seven entries,
all of which are ongoing tooling rather than one-off verification, so the
distinction is being maintained by taste.

Suggested shape, small:

- a line in CONTRIBUTING's testing guidance distinguishing migration-time
  verification from ongoing checks, with the test: if the artifact compares
  against a moving reference such as `origin/main` or a prior revision, its
  result belongs in the commit message and the script does not belong in the
  tree;
- and the corollary that what *does* belong is whatever keeps the migration from
  being undone — in this case an invariant that no module decides ownership
  itself, which keeps meaning something indefinitely.

Not proposing a lint. `scripts/` is small enough that the guidance is the whole
mechanism.

title: Converge flake.nix on its declared alejandra formatter and gate it
description:
`flake.nix` declares `formatter = alejandra`, but the committed file is not alejandra-formatted: running `nix fmt flake.nix` rewrites the entire `pages` derivation block (about 80 lines of indentation churn) that no one intended to touch.

That makes the formatter unusable for a narrow change — a contributor who runs it produces a diff dominated by unrelated reformatting, and one who does not leaves the tree divergent from its own declared formatter. During bd-185516 the reformat had to be reverted and three edits re-applied by hand to keep the diff reviewable.

Fix shape: one deliberate `nix fmt` commit that formats the tree, then a CI check (`nix fmt -- --check`) so it stays converged. The formatting commit should land on its own so it never mixes with behavioural changes.

title: docs/integration.md example fails without credentials for the provider it names
description:
`docs/integration.md` is the document a client integrator follows, and its opening example cannot be run as written without a prerequisite the page never states.

The example names `model: { provider: "github-copilot", id: "gpt-5-mini" }`. Opening a session validates that credentials exist for the named provider before any turn is attempted, so an integrator with no `auth.json` entry for it gets:

```
ProtocolResponseError: failed to open logical session
  cause: PiAdapterError: authentication is not configured for provider: github-copilot
```

Confirmed empirically while writing the consumer acceptance in bd-d54659; the harness had to seed a fixture key for the named provider before the documented request shape would open.

`docs/quickstart.md` does cover `auth.json` as an operator concern, but `integration.md` neither states the prerequisite nor links to it, and the two pages address different readers: quickstart is for someone running the daemon, integration is for someone writing a client against it. The first thing a Cacophony integrator does with this page fails, and the error names a provider rather than a missing setup step.

Fix is a short prerequisite note in `integration.md` stating that opening a session requires credentials for the provider it names, with a link to the quickstart section that establishes them. No code change.

title: [broken-on-main] Dash browser smoke gate fails on the CI runner at browser startup
description:
The `Dash browser smoke` job added in bd-c08a07 fails on the self-hosted CI runner while the identical command passes locally from the same Nix shell.

All three `@smoke` scenarios fail at browser startup, not on any assertion. From the uploaded `dash-smoke-playwright` artifact for run 30412617437 (commit 0692906), every error-context.md reports:

    Error: browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed

The preceding step, `nix develop .#e2e --command npm ci --ignore-scripts`, succeeded, and the browser-revision preflight is inside the failing script, so the bundle itself resolved. Locally `just dash-e2e-smoke` passes in 48-53s on the same commit and the same nixpkgs Playwright driver.

Leading hypothesis: the runner executes as root or in a container without user namespaces, so Chromium's sandbox aborts at launch. That is the standard cause of this exact message on self-hosted Linux runners, and it explains why a normal-user local run is unaffected. A `/dev/shm` size limit is the other common cause with the same signature.

Do not simply disable the sandbox globally. Preferred order:
1. Read the completed job log for Chromium's own stderr, which usually names the cause outright ("Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported").
2. If it is the sandbox, gate the relaxation behind an explicit CI-only environment variable consumed by playwright.config.ts launch options, documented in docs/dash-e2e.md, so a developer machine never silently runs an unsandboxed browser.
3. If it is /dev/shm, prefer raising the runner's shared memory over disabling the sandbox.

Until this is fixed the smoke gate is red on main for reasons unrelated to any change under review, which is precisely the failure mode the bd-c08a07 assessment argued against. Priority is therefore P1: a permanently red gate is worse than no gate.

Note main also shows pre-existing failures on Node 22.19.0, Node 24, and Nix (macOS) from at least d93900d, which are separate from this and predate the smoke job.

title: Make Nix-on-Droid package builds avoid native npm double-free
description: Operator reproduced Pi Daemon package failure during Astra/SGU24 nix-on-droid switch. Collective previously documented the npm double-free as resolved only by building off-device and pulling from cache, but the cache miss for pi-daemon d18854f exposed the native fallback. Make the Pi Daemon Nix consumer/package contract Nix-on-Droid-safe: avoid native npm execution on Android (prefer deterministic off-device/cross-built or reusable fixed package artifact), preserve exact package/lock integrity, and provide an actionable cache/prebuild path. Validate aarch64-linux package output and Nix-on-Droid module evaluation for Astra/SGU24 without weakening Linux/macOS checks. Document the platform contract and failure recovery. title: Make source-text assertions tolerate layout so formatting cannot turn main red
description:
A formatting-only Nix change turned `main` red because `test/release.test.mjs`
asserts the exact source text of `flake.nix`:

    assert.match(flake, /pages = pkgs\.runCommand "pi-daemon-pages"/);

Alejandra wraps that onto two lines, so a change with no semantic effect broke a
test. Fixed in bd-d79ef1 by matching the semantic fact instead of the layout,
but the pattern is broader than this one line.

Several tests assert repository source text with regexes: `release.test.mjs`
over `flake.nix` and workflow files, `chat-pane-layout.test.ts` over component
sources, `npm-deps-hash.test.mjs` and `nix-format.test.mjs` over `flake.nix`,
`Justfile`, and CI yaml. These are genuinely useful — they are how the repository
gates wiring and structure that has no runtime surface — but each one silently
couples a formatter, a linter, or a reviewer's whitespace preference to a
passing suite.

Suggested shape, in rough order of value:

1. A short convention note in CONTRIBUTING: when asserting source text, assert
   the semantic fact and tolerate layout. Prefer parsing over regex where a
   parser already exists, for example `JSON.parse` for `package.json` rather
   than a regex over its text; several tests already do this and are the model.
2. Where layout tolerance is impractical, make the assertion name the coupling
   in a comment so the next formatter change has a pointer.

Not proposing removing the assertions. The gap is that nothing tells an author
the coupling exists until CI goes red.

title: Prove the packaged binary serves without creating a process
description:
Extends bd-c4c80b from the code to the artefact. That acceptance runs `dist/cli.js`; a Cacophony deployment installs the Nix package and its Home Manager service runs `.../bin/pi-daemon serve`. `nix/home-manager-module-check.nix` proves the generated service *configuration* is right and never launches it, so nothing had established that the packaged binary serves at all.

Opt-in, because building the package runs the full suite in `checkPhase` and takes minutes, which the deterministic gate must not depend on. It builds nothing itself: point `PI_DAEMON_PACKAGE_ROOT` at an existing `nix build .#pi-daemon` result so the acceptance measures the artefact rather than the build.

Two environment assumptions surfaced while writing it, both of which failed only outside the developer machine and are worth recording because they are the same class:

1. The process-table walk shelled out to `ps`, which the Nix build sandbox does not provide — `spawn ps ENOENT`, exactly the shape of the `openssl` dependency that broke the Node CI lane. Fixed by reading `/proc` where it exists and keeping `ps` only as the macOS fallback, which removes the dependency rather than declaring it.
2. The auth fixture named a provider literally. That matched by accident locally and failed in the sandbox with "no authenticated Pi model is available". It now derives the provider from the SDK's own model registry, so the fixture cannot drift from what the SDK actually knows.

Verified end to end: `nix build .#pi-daemon` succeeds with the new test in the sandbox, and the packaged binary serves two logical sessions and gains no descendant process.

title: [broken-on-main] Browser smoke gate still fails at launch; capture the browser's own stderr
description:
Follow-up to bd-df1c84, which was the wrong fix. The `Dash browser smoke` job still fails on the self-hosted runners with all three scenarios reporting

    Error: browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed

on run 30419966285 (commit 419c750), which already contains the sandbox relaxation landed at 7843343.

What is now ruled out:

- Environment passthrough. `PI_DAEMON_E2E_NO_SANDBOX` does reach the config through `nix develop .#e2e --command`, verified directly: `PI_DAEMON_E2E_NO_SANDBOX=1 nix develop .#e2e --command node -e '...'` prints `"1"`. So `--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage` were applied and the browser still died at launch.
- The browser bundle itself. The revision preflight passes in the job, and the same bundle runs the suite locally.

So neither the Chromium sandbox nor `/dev/shm` sizing explains it, and the cause is still unknown. Note the runners vary between runs: `pi-daemon-ms-dev-4` for run 30412617437 and `pi-daemon-ms-dev-3` for 30419966285, so this is not one bad host.

The blocker is diagnostic, not analytical: Playwright swallows the browser's own stderr unless `DEBUG=pw:browser` is set, so every failure so far reports the symptom and none report the cause. Guessing again would be a third round trip on a gate that is already red.

Proposal: add a `web/scripts/check-browser-launch.mjs` preflight that launches Chromium with the same launch options the suite uses, and on failure prints the browser's own stderr and exit status rather than Playwright's generic message. Run it alongside the existing revision preflight in `e2e:nix` and `e2e:smoke`. Two benefits beyond this incident: the job fails in seconds with a self-describing message instead of three identical scenario failures two minutes in, and a contributor whose machine cannot launch the browser gets told why.

Then read the next run's log and fix the actual cause.

Note the smoke job is not the only red on main: bd-7cba4b (openssl on the Node lane) is still open and unowned, so main CI is red regardless of this bead.

Creation must be lazy: it may persist a validated dormant/catalog session or browser draft, but must not instantiate an AgentSessionRuntime, load SDK/provider/model/extensions/tools, acquire a controller, spawn a process, or submit work before the user sends the first message. The new pane should look like an ordinary empty conversation with the composer pinned to the pane bottom and an inline `first message starts this session` indicator. First send atomically materializes/hydrates the session through normal policy, obtains controller state, and admits exactly one prompt; retries must obey existing idempotent/indeterminate semantics and must never duplicate the first turn. Define the neutral backend/BFF/API contract needed for embedded and dedicated modes, enforce cwd/root/resource bounds and service/browser auth separation, and add acceptance proving zero runtime/SDK/model work before send, exactly one runtime+turn after send, refresh/restart durability, cancellation of an unsent draft, and no subprocess creation. Operator report 2026-07-19; current Sidebar has no create action and ordinary POST session currently opens a runtime immediately, so this requires an explicit lazy lifecycle rather than wiring the existing eager create blindly.

bead.title: Detect and repair pid-healthy but HTTP-dead Dash services
bead.description:
The Home Manager `daemon-main` API and web processes can remain pid/listener-healthy while returning no HTTP bytes indefinitely. This leaves Dash dead but launchd sees both jobs as running and never repairs them.

INCIDENT 2026-08-01, ordinary daemon-main only (Cacophony-owned instance was separate and unaffected):
- API PID60662 and web PID62145 had run for ~3 days and both listened on 127.0.0.1:7463/7465
- curl connected but received no response before 5-10s bounds; /dash was unusable
- both processes showed 0 CPU and no new readiness/fatal log entry
- web ignored SIGTERM for 30s and retained PID/listener state; required job-local `launchctl kickstart -k`
- API daemon accepted SIGTERM and emitted host_draining at 2026-08-01T23:18:14Z; launchd replaced it with PID62123
- under host pressure, daemon did not bind/ready until 23:21:11Z (~177s), host instance 4f9d50bd, zero retained/recovery failures
- web initially saw remote_unavailable, then launchd replacement PID68897 emitted web_ready at 23:22:58Z
- post-repair: /dash HTTP200 in 0.366s; API root expected HTTP401 in 0.040s
- Cacophony-owned PID65432/socket was not touched and remained running

HOST CONDITIONS (important reproducer, not an excuse to report healthy): root filesystem 922/927GB used, only 5.4GB available (100% in df display); load ~60-76; stock Pi sessions 4.3GB. The replacement eventually recovered without deleting data once load progressed.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. service health must distinguish pid/listener existence from bounded HTTP/API responsiveness;
2. a wedged component gets a bounded, instance-scoped recovery that never touches another Pi Daemon instance;
3. recovery preserves graceful drain where it works, but has an audited bounded escalation for an event loop that cannot process SIGTERM;
4. startup/readiness diagnostics expose the stage responsible for multi-minute delay instead of showing only a running PID;
5. supervision must not form a restart storm under disk/load pressure; one recovery attempt plus explicit degraded state is preferable;
6. tests cover TCP-accepting/no-response and a web process waiting on an unavailable API.
